proposal.description: The prescaler resets to its terminal count instead of 0, so the first millisecond tick comes on the first clock after reset instead of after a full PRESCALE_VAL period
proposal.reason: After rst_n is released, timestamp_ms becomes 1 on the first clock instead of after PRESCALE_VAL clocks. Every later value is reached PRESCALE_VAL-1 clocks early, so each fault-log timestamp reads one millisecond high for most of each period.

proposal.description: The millisecond counter resets to 1, as if the first millisecond were numbered 1, instead of 0
proposal.reason: timestamp_ms reads 1 during reset and right after it, not 0, and every later value is one higher than elapsed milliseconds. It wraps to 0 one tick early.

proposal.description: An explicit wrap of the millisecond counter compares against all-ones minus one, so it wraps from 2**TIMESTAMP_W-2 back to 0 and never shows all-ones
proposal.reason: At the tick after timestamp_ms reaches 2**TIMESTAMP_W-2, the output goes to 0 instead of all-ones. The wrap period is one millisecond short of 2**TIMESTAMP_W, and the all-ones value never appears.
